newsitem.title: UK: UK June house prices +1.5 percent - Nationwide.
newsitem.headline: UK June house prices +1.5 percent - Nationwide.

text.p: UK house prices rose a seasonally adjusted 1.5 percent in June, the sharpest monthly rise since March 1995 when there was an increase of 1.6, the Nationwide Building Society said on Friday.

Prices are now 11.0 percent higher than a year ago, the highest annual gain since the third quarter of 1989, when the increase was 15.5 percent. The Nationwide only published quarterly, not monthly figures then.
The unadjusted monthly index rose to 118.1 in June, from 116.1 in May and compared with 106.4 in June 1996.
The average price for houses in June increased to 59,189 stg from 58,196 in May.

But the Nationwide said the apparent strength of prices belies a flat trend in national property transactions and a heavily polarisation in the pattern of regional prices. The strongest increases are still in the south-east of England, particularly London.

But the July 2 budget will be crucial in determining what happens next in the housing market, particularly if Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown opts to reduce mortgage interest relief at source (MIRAS). Recent rises in UK interest rates are also a threat.
"The recovery, in its early stages in many parts of the country, could still be undermined," Paul Sanderson, Nationwide's head of research said.

"There are now tentative signs that the market is changing. In contrast to most of the rest of the country, house sales in London are continuing to rise at a brisk pace, suggesting supply constraints are being overcome to some extent," he said.

He added that higher prices were forcing first-time buyers to consider flats and small houses again, easing demand pressures further up the market. These factors should eventually led to a moderation in house price increases in the capital.

"Areas adjacent to London are now seeing stronger price rises as the recovery ripples outwards. In time we expect this to be reflected in a stronger trend in house sales in these areas, as already seen in the capital," he said.

The level of new mortgage approvals is showing a modest pick-up in activity following the flat trend seen in the first few months of this year, he said. "We expect this to continue as the market recovery broadens," he added.
